claims.statement: Tom Allen was timekeeper at the Standard when D. McMillan stayed fifteen minutes with Muldoon at Greco-Roman wrestling.
Tom Allen seconded Arthur Flint in Flint's prize fight against Hugh McManus near St. Clair, Missouri, on April 16, 1888.
Tom Allen was among those present at the fight near St. Clair, Missouri, on April 16, 1888.
Tom Allen backed Artie Flint in Flint's fight against Hugh McManus near St. Clair, Missouri, on April 16, 1888.
Tom Allen seconded Flint in the prize fight against McManus near St. Clair, Missouri.
Tom Allen told Flint to stay in his own corner and not go over to McManus's corner, but Flint did not follow the advice.
Tom Allen said Flint had inflicted more punishment on McManus than McManus had inflicted on Flint.
Tom Allen threw up the sponge for Flint, ending the fight.
According to the Daly side, Tom Allen was knocked down by Dan Daly in a street fight at Seventh and Market streets, St. Louis, on June 17, 1888.
According to the Daly party, Tom Allen was knocked out and asked Dan Daly to quit.
Tom Allen said Bob Farrell tripped him while Dan Daly and a crowd kicked him while he was down.
Tom Allen claimed one of three men who had been calling him names was in Dan Daly's saloon.
Tom Allen was said to have accused Dan Daly of doing things to hurt his business.
Tom Allen, a middleweight, was one of five prize-fighters whom Dr. Mathew D. Field brought before the New York Neurological Society to have their ears examined.
Tom Allen and Dan Daly made a wager on October 16, 1888, depending on a gloved match between Dan Daly and Hugh McManus set for December 1888.
A temporary stakeholder said Daly's money was up on time and was turned over to Bill Clark, disputing Allen's forfeit claim.
Tom Allen's interference with the Daly-McManus prize fight drew a protest from Deacon Hovser's paper, which said the fight should go on.
Tom Allen backed Hugh McManus in the match against Dan Daly and claimed a $750 forfeit for him.
Tom Allen claimed a forfeit at noon on December 5, 1888, saying Daly's final $250 deposit was not up.
Asked about Sullivan and Kilrain, Allen said Kilrain could not whip Sullivan with a baseball bat (the year is printed as 1839; the match was in 1889).
Tom Allen was at the ringside when Sullivan and Kilrain fought with bare fists at Richburg.
Tom Allen said Kilrain would beat Sullivan and that he would place his money on Kilrain.
Tom Allen said he was for Kilrain when asked for his opinion before the Sullivan-Kilrain fight.
Tom Allen said Kilrain's condition was good but that he would like him better if he were not so fat.
Tom Allen said Jake Kilrain would win his fight with John L. Sullivan.
Tom Allen, Joe Coburn and Tom Kelly all agreed that Jake Kilrain would win the fight with John L. Sullivan.
Tom Allen and Tom Kelley favored the Police Gazette's alleged champion, Jake Kilrain, over John L. Sullivan.
Tom Allen backed Jake Kilrain against John L. Sullivan at Richburg, Miss., about two years before this article, on Charlie Mitchell's judgment.
Edward Smith was to be Tom Allen's guest for a few days.
Tom Allen wrote that a Sioux boxer would be unlikely to become a pugilist and would kick and bite like a savage once he began to take punishment.
Tom Allen, with Tom Kelly, thought Tommy Ryan would beat Danny Needham and preferred Peter Maher to Bob Fitzsimmons, though doubtful of the latter result.
Tom Allen tried to place money on Maher before his fight with Fitzsimmons, but could not find anyone to take it.
Tom Allen said he saw the Fitzsimmons-Maher fight.
Tom Allen accompanied Charley Mitchell into the ring at the Olympic Club, New Orleans, with Frank Slavin and Pat Allen, before Mitchell's sparring bout.
Tom Allen was waiting in the Southern Hotel rotunda on March 5, 1892, to take Frank P. Slavin out for a spin.
Tom Allen was present in Charles Mitchell's room at the Southern Hotel on March 5, 1892, when Mitchell dictated his reply to John L. Sullivan's challenge.
Tom Allen held his birthday celebration with friends at his headquarters on Market street, St. Louis.
Tom Allen is a Slavin man and wants to place a few dollars on Frank Slavin to win.
Tom Allen is a Slavin man and is more positive than Kelly that Frank Slavin will prove the victor.
Tom Allen is now with John L. Sullivan and will back him whenever an opportunity presents itself.
Tom Allen predicted Sullivan would win in 20 to 30 rounds, McAuliffe in 25 rounds and Dixon in 10 rounds in the New Orleans fights of September 1892.
Tom Allen quoted betting odds of 7 to 4 on Sullivan, 5 to 4 on McAuliffe and 3 to 1 on Dixon for the New Orleans fights.
Tom Allen does not recognize Corbett as John L. Sullivan's superior.
Tom Allen was very positive that John L. Sullivan would win.
Fred Watkins, Allen's old backer, was in the St. Louis delegation at New Orleans.
Tom Allen was at ringside in New Orleans for the McAuliffe-Myer fight at the Olympic Athletic Club, as one of the two most noted St. Louisans present.
Tom Allen said Sullivan lost to Corbett because he was unfit to enter the ring and was overweight.
Tom Allen said Corbett won his fight with Sullivan squarely and deserves credit for it.
The Post-Dispatch answered a reader that Tom Allen never fought Jem Mace.
Tom Allen said he would see that Frank 'Dutch' Neil's stake (printed as $590) was posted for a proposed finish fight with Johnnie Daly.
Tom Allen received a letter from Charley Mitchell, dated London, Nov. 7, about Mitchell's coming fight with Corbett.
Ed Smith (printed as 'EP SmiTH'), the Denver heavyweight, and his brother Paddy spent a few days with Tom Allen last week.
A New York writer said Joe Goddard was no more a prize fighter in the modern sense than Tom Allen was.
